title: Where the Relationship Addition Enters a Late Payment Fee Correction
content:
Whether the relationship addition enters the correction of a late payment fee on a card under Personal Credit Cards, and at which point it enters, turns on how long the card account has been open and on the money the cardholder moves through Personal Checking.

*Where the card account has been open at least 60 whole months and Piedmont Crescent Bank checking deposits posted to the cardholder's checking accounts in the last six months total at least 12000.00 USD* — the relationship addition is added to the fee as billed first and the credited share acts on that total.

*Where the card account has been open at least 60 whole months and those deposits total less than 12000.00 USD* — the credited share acts on the fee as billed alone and the relationship addition is added to the product afterwards.

*Where the card account has been open less than 60 whole months* — the credited share acts on the fee as billed alone and no relationship addition is made.

**Why the two conventions give different money.** On hypothetical figures of a fee as billed of 40.00 USD, a credited share of 50 percent and a relationship addition of 4.00 USD, the first convention works on 44.00 USD and yields 22.00 USD, while the second works on 40.00 USD and yields 24.00 USD; the third yields 20.00 USD. The order is therefore part of the rule and not a matter of presentation.

**On the boundaries.** The age of the account is read as at least: an account open exactly 60 whole months falls with the accounts open at least 60 whole months, and one open 59 whole months falls with the younger accounts, whatever the deposits show. The deposit figure is likewise read as at least: deposits of exactly 12000.00 USD in the last six months fall in the first case, and deposits of 11999.00 USD in the second.
